clearedSpotChecks.check: Which release the Tempo endpoint runs, and whether a later release is published (bracket of the session's RPC use).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Queried rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz on 2026-11-27: web3_clientVersion returned tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and eth_chainId returned 0x1079 (4217). The index at https://download.tempo.xyz/binaries/ lists v1.19.0 and v1.19.1 as its newest entries and nothing later. So the binaries the unit lifted are the release the public endpoint runs today. The answer covers one public RPC node only; other validators of the network are not visible through it, which the item does not claim otherwise.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Identity of the two binaries (Task 1): build id, compiler and linker, symbols and debug information, and the evm2 and ruint versions named in them.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d67483a4c21c39cd84d019a45c877ba792c8e2/Cargo.lock: evm2 is pinned to git rev 35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f and ruint is 1.21.1 with checksum a0de3fa9b4dac39cc2bd65679bacf9f531899d933605e2963b40c2129cdb55f2, as the item states. The ruint version is past the 1.21.0 mul_mod fault, and the unit's planted reproduction of that fault (skip test turned from < into <=) is caught by its vectors, so the tests can see that class of error. The build ids and compiler strings were not re-read by this verifier because the binaries were not opened again.

clearedSpotChecks.check: What the results mean for the PoolManager source on Tempo (all networks except Tempo are not affected by this unit).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read the cited lines: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 computes mulmod(a, b, not(0)) and :48 mulmod(a, b, denominator); src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14 uses div and mod, :26 div; src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:19-25 uses signextend, sdiv, smod and slt. Every one of these opcodes appears in results/arith_a64_summary.json byOp for all three dispatch families with 0 mismatches (MULMOD 134,453 each, ADDMOD 35,896, SDIV 5,860, SMOD 5,860, SIGNEXTEND 7,921, SAR 11,693, BYTE 7,921), and the jump destination result files show 0 mismatches for NEON and for the x86 scalar, SSE4.1, AVX2 and AVX-512 VBMI kernels with planted faults detected. The conclusion is scoped correctly: it rests on the unit's own instruction models of the shipped code, and it does not cover KECCAK256, TLOAD, TSTORE, MCOPY or CALLDATALOAD handlers, which the unit lists as an open lead. No contradiction found.
